blocks.text: Managing Slack for community managers on Mac

Community managers often feel buried in communication. You spend a large portion of your day monitoring channels and responding to members. On a Mac, the Slack desktop app is your primary hub. You need to master the interface to avoid losing time on repetitive clicks. The app requires macOS 14 or later to run the latest version, 4.47.59 or above.

Start by using keyboard shortcuts. Press Command + / to see the full list of commands. Use Command + K to open the Quick Switcher. This lets you jump to any conversation instantly. If you feel overwhelmed by the volume of messages, use the Threads view to keep discussions contained. You can open this view by pressing Command + Shift + T.

Lazur helps you stay in the flow. Hold Option + Command to ask about any setting or UI element you see on your screen. If you are stuck, ask Lazur to point at the preferences menu. It will draw a circle around the correct icon. You can also ask Lazur to guide you through complex tasks like setting up a new channel or configuring notification schedules. When you need to send a long update, hold the fn key to dictate your message. Lazur formats the text for you at the cursor.

Constant pings are the enemy of deep work. Community managers often have too many channels active. Open your preferences with Command + , to manage your alerts. You can set up a notification schedule so you only receive pings during your working hours. If a specific channel is too busy, right click the channel name and select Mute. This keeps the messages in your list but stops the desktop banners from appearing.

items: Use /dnd to pause all notifications for a set time.
Set custom notification keywords to be alerted only when your name or specific topics appear.
Use the Unreads view to see only what matters to you at the end of the day.
Clear your status when you step away to manage expectations about your availability.

blocks.text: You should treat your Slack workspace like a task manager. Star your most important channels to keep them at the top of your sidebar. Use the Save for Later feature to bookmark messages that require a follow up. You can view these items by clicking the Saved items icon in the top left. Many managers also use tools like SupaSidebar or Rambox to separate their brand accounts from their personal ones. This prevents the common mistake of posting a community response in the wrong workspace.

Do not leave every channel active. You will miss important mentions if your sidebar is cluttered with noise. Another common mistake is ignoring thread replies. If you reply in the main channel, you break the conversation flow. Always use the reply button to keep the channel clean. Finally, check your data retention settings. On the free plan, messages are only visible for 90 days. If you have important community feedback, copy it to a separate document or note app immediately.

faq.question: How do I move faster in Slack on my Mac?
faq.answer: Use keyboard shortcuts like Command + K for the Quick Switcher and Command + N for new messages. You can also use Lazur to dictate text or ask for help with settings by holding the shortcut keys.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Slack for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It can point to buttons on your screen or guide you through a process one step at a time.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle too many notifications?
faq.answer: Open your Slack preferences with Command + , and set a notification schedule. You can also mute busy channels and use the Unreads view to prioritize important mentions.
